summary_short: Krishna begins His teachings by explaining the eternal nature of the soul and the path of wise action.
summary_medium: Seeing Arjuna overwhelmed with grief, Krishna corrects his confusion. He explains that the soul is eternal and cannot be destroyed. Krishna introduces Sankhya—the knowledge of the Self—and lays the foundation of Karma Yoga, teaching how to act without attachment to results.
summary_detailed: This chapter marks the beginning of Krishna’s direct teaching to Arjuna.
Krishna explains that grief arises from misunderstanding the true nature of life and death.
He teaches that the soul (Atman) is eternal, indestructible, and beyond birth and death.
Krishna introduces the wisdom of Sankhya, distinguishing the body from the soul.
He emphasizes the importance of performing one’s duty without attachment to outcomes.
The chapter also describes the qualities of a person with steady wisdom (Sthitaprajna).
This chapter forms the philosophical foundation of the entire Bhagavad Gita.
what_you_learn: The difference between the body and the soul.
Why death should not be feared.
How to act with wisdom and detachment.
The qualities of a calm and wise person.
How clarity arises through right understanding.
